title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 207
paragraphs: Such were their intentions. Meanwhile the Greeks at Thermopylae, when the Persian drew near the pass, grew afraid and deliberated about retreating from their position. The rest of the Peloponnesians thought it best to fall back to the Peloponnese and hold the Isthmus as a guard; but Leonidas, when the Phokians and Locrians objected indignantly to this view, cast his vote for staying there and at the same time sending messengers to the various states, asking them to come up and help, since they were too few to repel the Median army.
